chapter: Porgy and Bess and Varsity Show
title: After the film: Canada, the lawyer Grossman and the break from Nazarro
summary: Bubbles places the final break with Nazarro after the Canada billing mix-up following Varsity Show, saying the lawyer Leonard Grossman helped get rid of him by 1943-44.

story.theme_name: Still working: current gigs, upcoming projects and plans
story.community_name: Managers, bookers and the business of getting work

blocks.x: Now, I'm going to tell you about -- now, we go to California to do the picture, did the picture "Varsity Show." I got the picture, okay? Now this is the time we come back to do -- this is the time when we go to Canada -- from here we go to Canada and get this mix-up where they put the case in court to break away from Nazzaro.
Was this directly after the picture.
It was all the segue, nothing was direct, all the segue; took time for all these things. If we did the picture here, we had to come back

to New York. I might take a month, it might take two months. Who knows? I didn't farm the time out, you understand? Therefore, we come back to New York from Canada and I related this to the lawyer that we had there, from there, who was Leonarday Grossman, was the attorney and he was the one that helped me get rid of Nazarro because I had all these things against him for the picture and the false billing and no advertising in Canada. I totaled that all up together and told him about it and got us rid of Nazarro.
Okay, so basically you were very dissatisfied with the way this picture went. After the "Varsity Show" you were very dissatisfied.
I was dissatisfied not the way the picture went, I was dissatisfied with all the things that had happened before

the picture and up to the picture. But this is the only time now. You see, I didn't know that he didn't send out the billing to the next engagement we had until after I got there in Canada. That's what I was trying to tell you. Well between that and working all night in a studio for Pathé, that was 1922, I waited all that time now and there was a time when -- and don't forget I always figured that was a put-up thing at Columbia Theater, it was put up that they wanted us in the theater. I think it was a put up thing to keep us with him. I think that's what it was.

However, my point in what I'm trying to tell you now is when we come back from Canada to relate this to a lawyer to get us in court to break this contract, that's the point that I was trying to bring to your attention that we got out of the contract with him at that point. It wasn't earlier when I was talking about in Chicago during '26, it wasn't then. It was farther down because in 1943 and '44 we
I take it that after "Varsity Show" you went to Canada to do a show and that was the last straw.
That was the straw that broke the camel's back.
That's right. That's right. That's what I'm talking about. That's when I started action against Nazarro.
